Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our offer for a price of €6.05 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. 

To give you some background on our current situation and market conditions, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost. Lastly, PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. 

Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days. We look forward to continuing our partnership with your team and supplying your needs from our extensive inventory.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

move.subject: Volume-tier offer for stainless bar supply
move.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for your offer and the explanation of the market movements behind it. We appreciate the inventory support, but would like the pricing to reflect the annual volume and a longer contractual commitment rather than the market movements alone.

Our proposal is for a binding annual quantity of 94800 kg over a 24-month contract. The attached monthly forecast gives you the demand profile for planning; please see the supporting figures below.

For this package, we propose EUR 4.88 per kg, payment at 90 days net and no price adjustment clause. Please review this as a dedicated volume-tier offer for the full contractual quantity, rather than standard stock pricing.

Can you confirm the volume-tier price you can offer on that basis?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Thank you very much for your message - it is always a pleasure to hear from you, and we are glad to help wherever we can.
We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.
Our terms: a price of €5.57 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 24 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.

A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price.

And while we are at it: our whole range is at your disposal, so if there is anything else on your list, just send it over - we are happy to quote.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

move.subject: Re: Bar stock pricing and annual volume commitment
move.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for the revised offer and for accepting 90-day payment and the 24-month term. I also appreciate that you checked the forecast and reflected it in your pricing.

To answer your volume question precisely: our proposal carries a binding annual quantity of 94800 kg over the 24-month contract. Please base the volume tier on that quantity; we are not proposing a higher annual commitment. The forecast already supplied sets out the demand profile.

I understand your concern about raw material volatility. However, the fixed-price alloy cover described in your letter provides a basis for reviewing the fixed-price approach, rather than ruling it out. Our purchase-order history also provides a concrete reference for this discussion; please see the figures below.

We can move our proposal to EUR 4.99 per kg, with 90 days net payment, a 24-month contract and no price adjustment clause. Please review this revised price against the committed annual quantity and confirm how far you can improve your offer on that basis.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

strategy:
Supplier: Edelstahl-Service Donautal (stainless bar stockholder, group company, inside sales desk). Its letter of
2026-07-06 says its nickel/alloy requirement is covered at fixed prices until March 2027. It always asks "Which volume
can you commit to?" and for the volume forecast; it will insert an AS-14404 index clause itself for a 24-month term
(let it - do not propose a clause yourself); it accepts 90-day payment when we hold it.
OBSERVED MECHANIC (4 sessions): its first reply is a package answer (about the same whatever our price). After that
it mirrors OUR price move: when we move up by ~0.11 EUR it moves down by ~0.11 (its cap); when we move by 0.01-0.02
it moves 0.03-0.05 and declares a final offer. It also goes final when we change nothing. So: anchor deep in round 1,
then move UP by about 0.10-0.12 EUR every round on the SAME package (no clause, 90 days, 24 months) with one new
verified claim each round, never touching payment or term, until the code closes. Our asks should stay below its
price each round; if the gap gets below 0.12, move to about 0.02 under its price.
Plan: ROUND 1 - state the binding fixed annual volume (case volume per year and the total over 24 months), attach
the forecast (attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite fc-latest; ask for the dedicated volume tier price. ONE sheet:
no index clause, 90 days, 24 months, level L10 (deepest). ROUND 2 - thank it for what it accepted, cite the
purchase-order claim, move up ~0.11 (pick the level closest to last price + 0.11, same package: if it inserted an
index clause, keep OUR package without clause - the supplier may keep offering the clause; that is fine).
ROUND 3 - cite PPI-C2431 fall (first window), move up ~0.11. ROUND 4 - cite the second PPI-C2431 window, move up
~0.11. ROUND 5 - no new claim, move up ~0.10, ask for its best price. Code accepts when it agrees or goes final.
Tone: warm, firm, concrete, short; one argument per sentence; mention its material cover until March 2027 once
(round 2) as the reason a fixed base price over the term is reasonable. Do NOT use any AS-14404 index claim and
do not use the scorecard claim.
